title: Choose how the Studio is laid out
question: Three ways to arrange Shruchi's editor around her live site. Every option has the same tools (pages, photos, sections, undo, phone preview); this choice is where they sit and how she reaches them.

options.label: Write on the page
options.lineage: document editors like Notion and Google Docs
options.thesis: The page itself is the editor: click any words and type, press + in the margin to add a block.
options.viewport: A thin top bar (page name, phone/desktop, undo, saved), then her real page edge to edge; a + in the left margin beside each block opens a small menu of block swatches; a block's options unfold in a card right beside it.
options.risk: The least visible tools of the three: photos, layout and page settings hide until she finds them.

options.label: The page fills the screen
options.thesis: The live page fills the screen; hover between sections for + Add section, click a block for its toolbar and a settings drawer.
options.viewport: Slim left icon rail (Pages, Add, Photos, Site, History, Help), the page large in the middle with the selected block outlined in oxblood and a floating toolbar, a settings drawer on the right showing that block's text, photo and layout choices.
options.risk: The settings drawer covers part of the page on a small laptop screen.

options.label: Sections in a list beside the page
options.thesis: A tidy list of the page's sections sits on the left like cards in a binder; open one to change it, drag to reorder, and the page on the right follows.
options.viewport: Top bar with the page picker; a left column listing Home's sections (Hero, Collections, Studies, Process, Every swatch) each as a punched card with a swatch thumbnail, the open one showing its settings inline; the live page on the right scrolled to it.
options.risk: More of her editing happens in the list than on the page itself, a step removed from what she sees.
